model.family: 2-layer bidirectional attention transformer (no LayerNorm), final-position MLP readout
model.condition: ch2 is constant 0 in the input distribution; tokens 0-10 are digits, 11/12/13 are operators, 14 is an end marker at position 6

author.notes: Each input has exactly one operator token (11='+', 12='-', 13='*') at position 1..4, digits 0..10 elsewhere, token 14 at position 6. The output is (left neighbour OP right neighbour) mod 11; the other digits are distractors. Verified 20000/20000 on inputs.pt.

variables.name: position of the operator token
variables.binding: lambda t: [i for i in range(7) if t[i] in (11, 12, 13)][0]

variables.name: operator (0='+' token 11, 1='-' token 12, 2='*' token 13)
variables.binding: lambda t: [x for x in t if x in (11, 12, 13)][0] - 11

variables.name: left operand (digit immediately before the operator)
variables.binding: lambda t: t[[i for i in range(7) if t[i] in (11, 12, 13)][0] - 1]

variables.name: right operand (digit immediately after the operator)
variables.binding: lambda t: t[[i for i in range(7) if t[i] in (11, 12, 13)][0] + 1]

variables.name: (a op b) mod 11
variables.binding: lambda t: (lambda p: ((t[p-1] + t[p+1]) % 11) if t[p] == 11 else (((t[p-1] - t[p+1]) % 11) if t[p] == 12 else ((t[p-1] * t[p+1]) % 11)))([i for i in range(7) if t[i] in (11, 12, 13)][0])

mechanisms.component: attn1+attn2 gather operator and its two neighbours into the final position; MLP (W_in/W_out) + residual direct path map to logits
mechanisms.output_fn: lambda v: (v['V_a'] + v['V_b']) % 11 if v['V_op'] == 0 else ((v['V_a'] - v['V_b']) % 11 if v['V_op'] == 1 else (v['V_a'] * v['V_b']) % 11)
mechanisms.description: Modular arithmetic mod 11 on the two digits adjacent to the single operator token. At resid_pre_mlp the operator is a clean rank-2 linear code; operands and partial result features (Fourier-like, op-dependent interactions such as a+b / a-b frequencies) are present but entangled; the MLP completes the computation.

summary.task: single-operator modular arithmetic mod 11: output = (a op b) mod 11 where op in {+,-,*} is the only operator token and a,b are its immediate neighbours
summary.edit_note: The requested +->- edit via W_in alone is only partially achievable for this network (~0.37 success at ~0.97 preservation in my tests); see report.md.
